text: Problem 2: Machine Learning Does Averages (20pts) Suppose we have data yy,...,y, € R and we want to choose a single value m € R which is “most repre- sentative” of our dataset. This is sometimes called the “cenral tendency” problem in statistics. A machine learning approach to this problem would measure how representative m is of the data using a loss function. (a) Consider the loss function L(m) = Y7, (yi — m)?. Show that L(m) is minimized by setting m = 5, where § = £ 0, i is the mean of our data. (b) Consider the loss function L(m) = max, |y; — m|. What value of m minimizes this loss? Hint: Using derivatives will not help here - try just thinking about the minimization problem directly. (c) Consider the loss function L(m) = Y7, [y — m|. Prove that L(m) is minimized by setting m to the median of the data. Hint: This question is harder than the previous two and takes some creativity! Again derivatives might not be helpful. (d) In a few short sentences, discuss when you might prefer each of the three losses above. Is the median typically considered a more “robust” measure of central tendency than the mean? Why?
